content.title: About
content.content: Liqueur cream is a sweet alcoholic beverage that combines a rich liqueur base with cream, sugar and flavorings. It has a velvety texture, a gentle creamy taste and the characteristic aroma of the chosen liqueur (e.g., coffee, chocolate, fruit).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Liqueur cream is often used as a dessert sauce, filling for cakes and ice‑cream.
In some countries, such as Italy, a similar product is called “crema di liquore” and is served with coffee.
Alcohol content is usually below 20 % ABV, giving it a milder taste than straight liqueurs.
Traditional recipes use brandy, cognac or rum as the alcoholic base.
There are many flavor variations: chocolate, coffee, berry, nut and more.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cream component provides calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Alcoholic bases often contain B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavorings based on cocoa, berries or spices can add antioxidant compounds.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: The alcohol content makes the product unsuitable for children, pregnant women and those abstaining from alcohol.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Cream and sugar make the cream energy‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The product contains dairy, which may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled as a dessert sauce, add to coffee, cocktails, ice‑cream, use as a pastry filling, or simply enjoy a spoonful.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a tightly sealed container. After opening, consume within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
